text:
carmen: Heads-up — eu-central1 GPUs are piling up on provisioning because a chunk of ephemeral NVMe on the scratch fleet is hitting sustained write stalls and occasional readonly remounts. seeing ~7-10% attach failures in the last 30m :grimacing:

devon: ack, noticed higher GPU pending count. any fsck/corruption alerts?

carmen: yes, small percentage of hosts reported kernel dmesg like `blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector ...` and overlayfs complained about writeback failures. quick nvme-cli on one node: ```bash
# nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
critical_warning: 1
media_errors: 3
error_count: 153
temperature: 55C
```

riley: that error_count is worrying. Is this a firmware cohort or just hot stripes? Region-wide or limited AZ?

carmen: concentrated in eu-central1-a and -b, ~120 hosts. Not fleet-wide. Janitor/ephemeral-cleaner has been ramping aggressive delete jobs there overnight — suspecting IO amplification from concurrent scrubs + high batch GPU allocations.

sanjay: any correlation with scratch cleaner window schedule? we recently shifted eu-central cleanup to 0100-0500 to reduce daytime thrash.

carmen: yes, timestamps line up. cleaner spike from 01:10 triggered scrub batches, overlapped with a big training job start at 01:15 that did a lot of short-lived heavy writes (checkpoint churn). result = write tail pressure and NVMe internal GC thrash.

maya: ops-bot shows a transient network blip at 01:13 too — could've increased IO latencies and forced retries. link: <https://internal/ops/incident/17670>

devon: two-pronged then: (1) IO amplification from concurrent background scrub + heavy checkpointing; (2) network hiccup magnifying retries. Both increase apparent wear and stall windows.

riley: immediate mitigation ideas?

carmen: proposed short-term actions:
- throttle janitor/cleaner cadence in eu-central for next 6 hours (reduce concurrency from 16 -> 4)
- enable temporary routing of new GPU attaches in eu-central to eu-west1 until scrub backlog reduces
- mark most impacted hosts as `drain:maintenance` so scheduler avoids them
- collect core dumps and run `fsck -y` on nodes with readonly remounts

sanjay: agreed. Throttle command: ```bash
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $INFRA_TOKEN' \n  -d '{"region":"eu-central1","service":"janitor","concurrency":4,"reason":"emergency throttle due to nvme write stalls"}' \n  https://infra-api.internal/v1/runner/config
```

maya: I'll run that now and kick a canary of 20 nodes to ensure attach success improves. ops-bot: please annotate the rollout.

ops-bot: janitor concurrency change applied to eu-central1: concurrency=4 by maya at 1767012360 :white_check_mark:

carmen: canary attach status after throttle: 18/20 succeeded, 2 failed with `attach timeout` (previously was ~45% fail). Good sign.

riley: schedule for reroute? we can shift new provisioning to eu-west1 for 2 hours, but that will increase cross-region egress and cost (estimated +8% for the training jobs). Are we OK with cost hit?

sanjay: short-term yes. prioritize availability. we'll run numbers later; flag finance for retrospective billing.

carmen: follow-ups:
- ops: run `smartctl`/`nvme-cli` collect on the 120 hosts and upload to /mnt/diag/euc1-nvme-thrash/1767012345
- eng-infra: add a temporary guard in the scheduler to avoid overlapping janitor scrubs with heavy checkpoint windows per customer (heuristic: if GPU attach backlog > 50 in region, defer high-concurrency scrubs)
- storage: open ticket with vendor for drives with media_errors > 0 and error_count delta > 50 in last 24h

riley: i'll add the scheduler guard as an emergency patch, small and feature-flagged. push window in 20m.

maya: ops-bot observed scrub job start times: 
`2026-03-21T01:09:43Z scrub-runner[pid=2211] shards=24 concurrency=16`
`2026-03-21T01:12:58Z training-job[job-id=xx] started checkpoint loop`

carmen: also saw one host with overlayfs checksum mismatch — ran `fsck -f` and remounted read-write, no data loss reported. keep watch list.

ops-bot: scheduler-reroute: moved 120 attach requests from eu-central1 -> eu-west1 at 1767012370 by maya :information_source:

sanjay: monitor metrics for next 2 hours: NVMe write latency p50/p95, attach success rate, scrub queue length, and GPU pending. Create dashboard and alert if attach success < 90% for 10m.

carmen: creating incident doc and will paste quick runbook steps there. Early root cause hypothesis: concurrent high-concurrency janitor scrubs + checkpoint-heavy workloads + transient network blip -> NVMe write amplification and internal GC thrash causing I/O stalls and readonly remounts on a subset of drives.

maya: thanks all. if we see more readonly remounts, start node-level replacement flow. I'll notify customer success for any impacted customers in the region.

riley: tldr: throttled cleaner, rerouted attaches, monitoring & scheduler guard in flight.

carmen: leaving notes here for postmortem: consider soft limits on janitor concurrency by region, auto-detect heavy write checkpoints and delay scrubs accordingly, and add early-warning metric for NVMe error_count deltas.

janitor-bot: scheduled backlog rescan to resume normal cadence at 2026-03-21T08:00:00Z (flagged as manual resume)

sanjay: nice work. will follow up with postmortem draft later today. :thumbsup:
